revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Square Mirrors
revealWordProblem.text:
The side lengths of two square mirrors are shown. Mirror A has sides of 2½ feet and Mirror B has sides of 1¾ feet.
Question: About how many times greater is the area of Mirror A than the area of Mirror B?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two square mirrors side by side: Mirror A is 2 and one-half feet across and Mirror B is 1 and three-fourths feet across.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each area first. Mirror A: 2½ × 2½ = 5/2 × 5/2 = 25/4 = 6¼ square feet. Mirror B: 1¾ × 1¾ = 7/4 × 7/4 = 49/16 = 3 1/16 square feet. Now divide to compare: 25/4 ÷ 49/16 = 25/4 × 16/49 = 400/196 ≈ 2.04. Mirror A's area is about 2.04 times as large as Mirror B's.

conceptIntro.heading: How do I divide one fraction by another fraction?
conceptIntro.intro: When you divide a fraction by a fraction, you keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (the divisor) to its reciprocal. Then multiply and simplify.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Dividing Fractions by Fractions. Formula: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c. 1. Name the question: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 asks how many 1/8s fit in 3/4. 2. Use common denominators: 3/4 = 6/8, and 6 eighths ÷ 1 eighth = 6. 3. Shortcut: multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor, 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6, then check by multiplying: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Agent Rivera has 3/4 pound and each portion is 1/8 pound. I want 3/4 ÷ 1/8.
It asks how many 1/8-pound portions fit in 3/4 pound. I rename 3/4 in eighths: 3/4 = 6/8.
6 eighths ÷ 1 eighth = 6, the same way 6 apples ÷ 1 apple = 6. That is the common-denominator method.
The reciprocal shortcut gives the same answer: 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6, because each pound holds 8 eighths. Check: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4. She can make 6 portions.
One more move to know: mixed number → improper fraction: multiply the bottom by the whole number, add the top, keep the same bottom. 3 1/2 → (2 × 3) + 1 = 7 → 7/2.
linesEs: El agente Rivera tiene 3/4 de libra y cada porción es de 1/8 de libra. Quiero 3/4 ÷ 1/8.
Pregunta cuántas porciones de 1/8 de libra caben en 3/4 de libra. Escribo 3/4 en octavos: 3/4 = 6/8.
6 octavos ÷ 1 octavo = 6, igual que 6 manzanas ÷ 1 manzana = 6. Ese es el método de denominadores comunes.
El atajo del recíproco da la misma respuesta: 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6, porque cada libra tiene 8 octavos. Compruebo: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4. Puede hacer 6 porciones.
Un movimiento más que debes saber: número mixto → fracción impropia: multiplica el denominador por el entero, suma el numerador y conserva el mismo denominador. 3 1/2 → (2 × 3) + 1 = 7 → 7/2.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's try 1/2 ÷ 1/4. How many 1/4s fit in 1/2? Rename 1/2 as 2/4.
2 fourths ÷ 1 fourth = 2. The reciprocal shortcut agrees: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2.
linesEs: 2 cuartos ÷ 1 cuarto = 2. El atajo del recíproco coincide: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2.

youDo.title: Your turn — a mixed number this time
lines: Try 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4. The first number is a mixed number, so it cannot be flipped or multiplied as it stands.
Rewrite it as an improper fraction: 2 1/2 = 5/2, because two wholes are 4 halves plus 1 more half.
Now multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor 1/4: 5/2 × 4/1 = 20/2.
Simplify: 20/2 = 10. So 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 10. Check by multiplying: 10 × 1/4 = 10/4 = 2 1/2 — ten quarter-pieces really do fill two and a half wholes.
linesEs: Prueba 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4. El primer número es un número mixto, así que no se puede invertir ni multiplicar tal como está.
Reescríbelo como fracción impropia: 2 1/2 = 5/2, porque dos enteros son 4 medios más 1 medio más.
Ahora multiplica por el recíproco del divisor 1/4: 5/2 × 4/1 = 20/2.
Simplifica: 20/2 = 10. Entonces 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 10. Comprueba multiplicando: 10 × 1/4 = 10/4 = 2 1/2: diez piezas de un cuarto llenan de verdad dos enteros y medio.

conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Dividir fracciones entre fracciones. Fórmula: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c. 1. Nombra la pregunta: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 pregunta cuántos 1/8 caben en 3/4. 2. Usa denominadores comunes: 3/4 = 6/8, y 6 octavos ÷ 1 octavo = 6. 3. Atajo: multiplica por el recíproco del divisor, 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6, y luego comprueba multiplicando: 6 × 1/8 = 6/8 = 3/4

El divisor (5/8) es la fracción que se convierte en su recíproco (8/5). ¿Cuál fracción volteó el detective en el Paso 2?

approaching.explanation: To find the reciprocal, flip the fraction. The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3.
choiceFeedback: That flips only the 3. A reciprocal flips the WHOLE fraction, so both the 3 and the 5 change places.
That is the original fraction, unflipped. A reciprocal swaps the top and bottom numbers, so 3/5 becomes 5/3.
The bottom number was used for both spots. Keep both numbers — just trade their places: the 3 moves down, the 5 moves up.
hints: Re-read 'reciprocal' — it's about the two numbers of the fraction trading places.
Swap the numerator (top number) with the denominator (bottom number). Nothing else changes.
In 3/5, the 3 is on top and the 5 is on the bottom. Trade their spots and match the result to a choice.
approaching.explanationEs: Para hallar el recíproco, invierte la fracción. El recíproco de 3/5 es 5/3.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer 'recíproco': se trata de que los dos números de la fracción cambien de lugar.
Intercambia el numerador (número de arriba) con el denominador (número de abajo). Nada más cambia.
En 3/5, el 3 está arriba y el 5 abajo. Intercambia sus lugares y compara el resultado con las opciones.

choiceFeedback: 1/8 is 1/2 × 1/4 — the divisor was never flipped. How many 1/4s fit in 1/2? Two: 1/2 = 2/4.
1/2 is 1/4 ÷ 1/2 — the dividend and divisor are switched. Ask how many 1/4s fit in 1/2.
4 is just the reciprocal of 1/4. Multiply it by the dividend: 1/2 × 4 = 2.
hints: This asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit inside 1/2 — the pieces are smaller than the amount.
Multiply by the reciprocal: keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4.
1/4 flips to 4/1, so multiply 1/2 × 4/1 across the tops and bottoms, then simplify your fraction.
approaching.explanationEs: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Dos pedazos de tamaño 1/4 caben en 1/2.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben dentro de 1/2: las piezas son más pequeñas que la cantidad.
Multiplica por el recíproco: conserva 1/2, cambia ÷ por × e invierte el divisor 1/4.
1/4 se invierte a 4/1, así que multiplica 1/2 × 4/1 arriba con arriba y abajo con abajo, y luego simplifica tu fracción.

choiceFeedback: 3/32 is 3/4 × 1/8 — the divisor was never flipped. Common denominators: 6/8 ÷ 1/8 = 6.
8/3 is not how many 1/8s fit in 3/4. Rename 3/4 as 6/8: 6 eighths ÷ 1 eighth = 6.
24 is 3 × 8 — the 4 in 3/4 was dropped. 3/4 × 8 = 24/4 = 6.
hints: How many 1/8-pieces fit into 3/4? Eighths are small, so expect several.
Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip 1/8 to its reciprocal.
Set up 3/4 × 8/1, multiply tops and bottoms, then simplify the product.
approaching.explanationEs: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8/1 = 24/4 = 6. Seis pedazos de tamaño 1/8 caben en 3/4.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas piezas de 1/8 caben en 3/4? Los octavos son pequeños, así que espera varias.
Conserva 3/4, cambia ÷ por × e invierte 1/8 a su recíproco.
Plantea 3/4 × 8/1, multiplica arriba y abajo, y luego simplifica el producto.

approaching.stem: What is the first step in evaluating 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
choices: Divide 2 by 1/4 and ignore the half
approaching.explanation: A mixed number cannot be flipped or multiplied as it stands, so rewrite it first: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Then multiplying by the reciprocal gives 5/2 × 4/1 = 10.
choiceFeedback: A mixed number has no single numerator and denominator to flip.
Dropping the half changes the problem into a different one.
Division is not solved by adding the parts.
hints: Which number in this problem is a mixed number?
How many halves are in 2 1/2?
Rewrite it as one fraction before multiplying by the reciprocal.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el primer paso para evaluar 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
approaching.explanationEs: Un número mixto no se puede voltear ni multiplicar tal como está, así que primero reescríbelo: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Luego, multiplicar por el recíproco da 5/2 × 4/1 = 10.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número de este problema es un número mixto?
¿Cuántos medios hay en 2 1/2?
Reescríbelo como una sola fracción antes de multiplicar por el recíproco.

approaching.instructions: Sort each division: will the quotient be GREATER than 1 or LESS than 1?
approaching.hint: Decide: does this expression ask 'how many fit' (quotient bigger) or something else?
hints: Work out each quotient first (multiply by the reciprocal), then compare that quotient to 1.
Quick check: when the dividend is bigger than the divisor, the quotient lands above 1.
First card: 3/4 ÷ 1/4 = 3. Is 3 more or less than 1? Place it, then repeat for each card.
approaching.explanation: Dividing asks how many copies of the divisor fit inside the dividend. In 3/4 ÷ 1/4, 5/6 ÷ 1/3, and 2/3 ÷ 1/6 the dividend is larger, so more than one copy fits and the quotient passes 1; in 1/4 ÷ 1/2, 1/3 ÷ 2/3, and 2/5 ÷ 4/5 the divisor is larger, so only part of a copy fits and each quotient is 1/2.
approaching.explanationEs: Dividir pregunta cuántas copias del divisor caben dentro del dividendo. En 3/4 ÷ 1/4, 5/6 ÷ 1/3 y 2/3 ÷ 1/6 el dividendo es mayor, así que cabe más de una copia y el cociente pasa de 1; en 1/4 ÷ 1/2, 1/3 ÷ 2/3 y 2/5 ÷ 4/5 el divisor es mayor, así que solo cabe parte de una copia y cada cociente es 1/2.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada división: ¿el cociente será MAYOR que 1 o MENOR que 1?
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su cociente, como 3/4 ÷ 1/4 = 3. Compara ese cociente con 1.
Revisión rápida: cuando el dividendo es mayor que el divisor, el cociente queda por encima de 1.
Primera tarjeta: 3/4 ÷ 1/4 = 3. ¿Es 3 más o menos que 1? Colócala y repite con cada tarjeta.

choiceFeedback: You have the dividend and divisor backward. Which is the whole, and which is the piece size?
2/9 is 2/3 × 1/3 — the divisor was never flipped. How many thirds are in 2/3? Two.
6 is 2 × 3 — the 3 in 2/3 was dropped. 2/3 × 3 = 6/3 = 2.
hints: Both fractions are thirds — you're counting how many 1/3-pieces sit inside 2/3.
With matching denominators, compare numerators — or multiply by the reciprocal to be sure.
Flip 1/3 to 3/1: 2/3 × 3/1. Multiply across, then simplify before answering.
approaching.explanationEs: 2/3 ÷ 1/3 = 2/3 × 3/1 = 6/3 = 2. Dos pedazos de tamaño 1/3 caben en 2/3.
hintsEs: Ambas fracciones son tercios: estás contando cuántas piezas de 1/3 caben dentro de 2/3.
Con denominadores iguales, compara los numeradores, o multiplica por el recíproco para asegurarte.
Invierte 1/3 a 3/1: 2/3 × 3/1. Multiplica y luego simplifica antes de responder.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: The student tried to divide the tops and bottoms straight across instead of using the reciprocal shortcut. Keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. (Even though the answer happens to be 2 here, dividing straight across is not a reliable rule — it breaks for problems like 2/3 ÷ 1/2.)
hints: You cannot divide fractions by dividing the numerators and denominators straight across.
Use the reciprocal shortcut: keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to its reciprocal 4/1.
approaching.explanation: In the second step the numerators and denominators were divided straight across, which is not how fraction division works. Keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4 to 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. The answer happens to match here, but straight-across dividing falls apart on a problem like 2/3 ÷ 1/2.
approaching.explanationEs: En el segundo paso se dividieron los numeradores y los denominadores en línea recta, y así no funciona la división de fracciones. Conserva 1/2, cambia ÷ por × y voltea el divisor 1/4 para obtener 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Aquí la respuesta coincide por casualidad, pero dividir en línea recta falla en un problema como 2/3 ÷ 1/2.
approaching.correctWorkEs: El estudiante intentó dividir los numeradores y denominadores directamente en lugar de usar el atajo del recíproco. Mantén 1/2, cambia ÷ a ×, y voltea el divisor 1/4 a 4/1: 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. (Aunque aquí la respuesta casualmente es 2, dividir directamente no es una regla confiable — falla en problemas como 2/3 ÷ 1/2.)
hintsEs: No puedes dividir fracciones dividiendo los numeradores y denominadores de forma directa.
Multiplica por el recíproco: mantén 1/2, cambia ÷ por × y voltea el divisor 1/4 a su recíproco 4/1.

onLevel.label: Divide each pair of fractions using the reciprocal shortcut.
onLevel.hint: For each row, calculate the quotient by dividing the whole by the piece size.
hints: The middle column already shows the multiplication by the reciprocal — like 1/2 × 6/1 = 6/2.
Your job is the last step: simplify each product fraction to its final quotient.
Row one ends at 6/2 — divide the top by the bottom to simplify, then do the same for every row.
onLevel.explanation: The middle column has already shows the multiplication by the reciprocal, so the last column is only the simplifying step: 6/2 = 3, 12/4 = 3, 6/3 = 2, and 20/8 = 2 1/2. Every quotient is more than 1 because each dividend holds more than one copy of its divisor.
onLevel.explanationEs: La columna del medio ya hizo la multiplicación por el recíproco, así que la última columna es solo el paso de simplificar: 6/2 = 3, 12/4 = 3, 6/3 = 2 y 20/8 = 2 1/2. Todos los cocientes son mayores que 1 porque cada dividendo contiene más de una copia de su divisor.
onLevel.labelEs: Divide cada pareja de fracciones usando el atajo del recíproco.
hintsEs: La columna del medio ya muestra la multiplicación por el recíproco, como 1/2 × 6/1 = 6/2.
Tu trabajo es el último paso: simplificar cada fracción producto hasta su cociente final.
La fila uno termina en 6/2: divide el número de arriba entre el de abajo para simplificar y haz lo mismo en cada fila.

onLevel.label: Match each fraction division to its quotient.
onLevel.hint: Match each fraction division to its answer. Divide the first number by the second.
hints: Flip only the SECOND fraction in each pair, then multiply across.
Simplify every product — some matches are whole numbers, some are mixed numbers like 2 1/2.
Start with 4/5 ÷ 2/5: the denominators match, so ask how many groups of 2 fifths fit into 4 fifths.
onLevel.explanation: Flipping only the second fraction and multiplying produces every match: 4/5 × 5/2 = 2, 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 2 1/2, 2/3 × 6/1 = 4, and 7/8 × 4/1 = 28/8 = 3 1/2. Only 1/2 ÷ 3/4 has a divisor larger than its dividend, which is why 2/3 is the one quotient below 1.
onLevel.explanationEs: Voltear solo la segunda fracción y multiplicar produce cada pareja: 4/5 × 5/2 = 2, 3/4 × 8/3 = 2, 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 2 1/2, 2/3 × 6/1 = 4 y 7/8 × 4/1 = 28/8 = 3 1/2. Solo 1/2 ÷ 3/4 tiene un divisor mayor que su dividendo, por eso 2/3 es el único cociente menor que 1.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada división de fracciones con su cociente.
hintsEs: Invierte solo la SEGUNDA fracción de cada pareja y luego multiplica.
Simplifica cada producto: algunas respuestas son números enteros y otras son números mixtos como 2 1/2.
Empieza con 4/5 ÷ 2/5: los denominadores coinciden, así que pregunta cuántos grupos de 2 quintos caben en 4 quintos.

onLevel.stem: A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. You only have a 1/6-cup scoop. How many scoops do you need?
choiceFeedback: Only 2 scoops of 1/6 cup makes 2/6 = 1/3 cup — not enough sugar. Use the reciprocal shortcut on 2/3 ÷ 1/6 and simplify what you get.
3 scoops of 1/6 cup make 3/6 = 1/2 cup — not enough. 2/3 = 4/6, so you need 4 scoops.
6 scoops of 1/6 cup make a whole cup — too much. 2/3 = 4/6, so you need 4 scoops.
hints: The recipe total is 2/3 cup; one scoop holds 1/6 cup — you're counting scoops, not multiplying.
Rewrite 2/3 in sixths so both amounts use the same size pieces.
Multiply top and bottom of 2/3 by 2 to get sixths, then count how many 1/6-scoops that makes.
onLevel.stemEs: Una receta necesita 2/3 de taza de azúcar. Solo tienes una cuchara medidora de 1/6 de taza. ¿Cuántas cucharadas necesitas?
hintsEs: El total de la receta es 2/3 de taza y una cuchara contiene 1/6 de taza: estás contando cucharadas, no multiplicando.
Reescribe 2/3 en sextos para que ambas cantidades usen piezas del mismo tamaño.
Multiplica arriba y abajo de 2/3 por 2 para obtener sextos y luego cuenta cuántas cucharadas de 1/6 forman.

onLevel.label: Place each quotient on the number line.
onLevel.hint: Solve each division. Then find the quotient on the number line.
hints: Calculate each quotient first: keep the dividend, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor, and simplify.
The line runs 0 to 6 by ones. Watch out: two of the targets land on the same tick.
Place A first: 1/2 ÷ 1/6 = 3, so the point goes on 3. Then check which other target shares that tick.
onLevel.explanation: Calculate before plotting: A = 1/2 × 6/1 = 3; B = 3/4 × 4/1 = 3; C = 2/3 × 3/1 = 2; D = 3/4 × 8/1 = 6. A and B share the tick at 3, C goes at 2, and D goes at 6.
onLevel.explanationEs: Calcula antes de marcar: A = 1/2 × 6/1 = 3; B = 3/4 × 4/1 = 3; C = 2/3 × 3/1 = 2; D = 3/4 × 8/1 = 6. A y B comparten la marca en 3, C va en 2 y D va en 6.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: The student changed ÷ to × but forgot to flip the divisor. Keep 2/3, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/2 to its reciprocal 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. The correct quotient is 4/3 (1 1/3), not 1/3.
hints: After you change ÷ to ×, you must also flip the second fraction (the divisor).
The divisor 1/2 should become its reciprocal 2/1 before you multiply: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.
onLevel.explanation: The step that changed ÷ to × left the divisor as 1/2 instead of flipping it, so the problem turned into multiplication of the original fractions. Multiplying by the reciprocal turns the divisor into 2/1, giving 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. That size makes sense, because 1/2 is smaller than 2/3, so more than one copy fits.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso que cambió ÷ por × dejó el divisor como 1/2 en vez de voltearlo, así que el problema se convirtió en una multiplicación de las fracciones originales. Multiplicar por el recíproco convierte el divisor en 2/1, lo que da 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque 1/2 es menor que 2/3, así que cabe más de una copia.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante cambió ÷ a × pero olvidó voltear el divisor. Mantén 2/3, cambia ÷ a ×, y voltea el divisor 1/2 a su recíproco 2/1: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3 = 1 1/3. El cociente correcto es 4/3 (1 1/3), no 1/3.
hintsEs: Después de cambiar ÷ por ×, también debes voltear la segunda fracción (el divisor).
El divisor 1/2 debe convertirse en su recíproco 2/1 antes de multiplicar: 2/3 × 2/1 = 4/3.

onLevel.stem: Agent Rivera filled 3/4 of an evidence bag, and that part weighs 3/8 pound. How much would a FULL bag weigh? (3/8 ÷ 3/4 asks how much is in one whole bag.)
onLevel.explanation: 3/4 of the bag is 3/8 pound, so 1/4 of the bag is 1/8 pound and the whole bag (4 fourths) is 4/8 = 1/2 pound. The shortcut agrees: 3/8 ÷ 3/4 = 3/8 × 4/3 = 12/24 = 1/2. Check: 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8.
choiceFeedback: 9/32 is 3/8 × 3/4 — that finds 3/4 OF the 3/8 pound. The 3/8 pound is already the 3/4 part, so the full bag weighs more.
2 divides in the wrong order (3/4 ÷ 3/8). The known weight, 3/8 pound, is the amount being divided.
1 1/8 adds 3/8 and 3/4. Find what one fourth of the bag weighs first, then build the whole bag.
hints: The 3/8 pound is only part of the bag. Which part?
If 3 fourths weigh 3/8 pound, what does 1 fourth weigh?
Multiply that by 4 for the whole bag, then check: 3/4 × your answer = 3/8.
onLevel.stemEs: La agente Rivera llenó 3/4 de una bolsa de evidencia, y esa parte pesa 3/8 de libra. ¿Cuánto pesaría la bolsa LLENA? (3/8 ÷ 3/4 pregunta cuánto hay en una bolsa entera.)
onLevel.explanationEs: 3/4 de la bolsa pesan 3/8 de libra, así que 1/4 de la bolsa pesa 1/8 de libra y la bolsa entera (4 cuartos) pesa 4/8 = 1/2 libra. El atajo coincide: 3/8 ÷ 3/4 = 3/8 × 4/3 = 12/24 = 1/2. Comprueba: 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8.
choiceFeedbackEs: 9/32 es 3/8 × 3/4: eso halla 3/4 DE los 3/8 de libra. Los 3/8 de libra ya son la parte de 3/4, así que la bolsa llena pesa más.
2 divide en el orden equivocado (3/4 ÷ 3/8). El peso conocido, 3/8 de libra, es la cantidad que se divide.
1 1/8 suma 3/8 y 3/4. Primero halla cuánto pesa un cuarto de la bolsa y luego arma la bolsa entera.
hintsEs: Los 3/8 de libra son solo una parte de la bolsa. ¿Qué parte?
Si 3 cuartos pesan 3/8 de libra, ¿cuánto pesa 1 cuarto?
Multiplica eso por 4 para la bolsa entera y comprueba: 3/4 × tu respuesta = 3/8.

onLevel.stem: The lab printer fills 2/5 of a box of evidence labels in 1/2 hour. At that rate, how much of a box does it fill in ONE hour?
onLevel.explanation: 2/5 ÷ 1/2 asks how much is in one whole hour. Half an hour fills 2/5 of a box, so a full hour (2 halves) fills 2 × 2/5 = 4/5 of a box. Shortcut: 2/5 × 2/1 = 4/5. Check: 1/2 × 4/5 = 4/10 = 2/5.
choiceFeedback: 1/5 is 2/5 × 1/2 — the amount for a quarter hour. An hour is twice as long as half an hour, so the printer fills more.
1 1/4 divides in the wrong order (1/2 ÷ 2/5). Divide the labels filled, 2/5, by the time, 1/2 hour.
9/10 adds 2/5 and 1/2. Two half-hours make an hour, so double the 2/5 instead.
hints: How many half-hours are in one hour?
Each half-hour fills 2/5 of a box.
onLevel.stemEs: La impresora del laboratorio llena 2/5 de una caja de etiquetas de evidencia en 1/2 hora. A ese ritmo, ¿cuánto de una caja llena en UNA hora?
onLevel.explanationEs: 2/5 ÷ 1/2 pregunta cuánto hay en una hora entera. Media hora llena 2/5 de una caja, así que una hora completa (2 medias horas) llena 2 × 2/5 = 4/5 de una caja. Atajo: 2/5 × 2/1 = 4/5. Comprueba: 1/2 × 4/5 = 4/10 = 2/5.
choiceFeedbackEs: 1/5 es 2/5 × 1/2: lo que llena en un cuarto de hora. Una hora es el doble de media hora, así que la impresora llena más.
1 1/4 divide en el orden equivocado (1/2 ÷ 2/5). Divide las etiquetas, 2/5, entre el tiempo, 1/2 hora.
9/10 suma 2/5 y 1/2. Dos medias horas forman una hora, así que duplica los 2/5.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas medias horas hay en una hora?
Cada media hora llena 2/5 de una caja.
2/5 ÷ 1/2 = 2/5 × 2. Comprueba: 1/2 × tu respuesta = 2/5.

extending.title: Find the Division Error
extending.correctWork: The student forgot to flip. 2/5 × 4/3 (flip the divisor 3/4 to get 4/3). Then 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.
hints: When you multiply by the reciprocal, which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (3/4) should become its reciprocal (4/3). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
extending.explanation: The reciprocal step swapped the operation but left the divisor as 3/4, so no fraction was actually flipped. The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3, so the problem is 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, not 3/10.
extending.explanationEs: El paso del recíproco cambió la operación pero dejó el divisor como 3/4, así que en realidad no se volteó ninguna fracción. El recíproco de 3/4 es 4/3, así que el problema es 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15, no 3/10.
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó voltear. 2/5 × 4/3 (voltea el divisor 3/4 para obtener 4/3). Entonces 2/5 × 4/3 = 8/15.
hintsEs: Al multiplicar por el recíproco, ¿cuál fracción se voltea?
El divisor (3/4) debe convertirse en su recíproco (4/3). ¿El Paso 2 volteó la fracción correcta?

extending.prompt: Is 3/4 ÷ 1/2 the same as 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Solve both and explain why or why not. What does this tell you about the order in division?
extending.sentenceFrame: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = ___ and 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = ___. These are ___ because ___. This shows that division is ___.
extending.hint: Explain how dividing by smaller fractions produces larger quotients using a real scenario.
hints: Don't assume the two divisions match — solve each one on its own first.
Use the reciprocal shortcut on both: flip the second fraction each time, then compare the two quotients.
First one: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 → 3/4 × 2/1. Work it out, then set up 1/2 ÷ 3/4 the same way and compare.
extending.explanation: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 becomes 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, while 1/2 ÷ 3/4 becomes 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, so the two expressions are not equal. Swapping the dividend and the divisor flips the quotient to its reciprocal, which shows that division is not commutative — order matters.
extending.explanationEs: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 se convierte en 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, mientras que 1/2 ÷ 3/4 se convierte en 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, así que las dos expresiones no son iguales. Intercambiar el dividendo y el divisor convierte el cociente en su recíproco, lo que muestra que la división no es conmutativa: el orden importa.
extending.promptEs: ¿Es 3/4 ÷ 1/2 lo mismo que 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Resuelve los dos y explica por qué sí o por qué no. ¿Qué te dice esto sobre el orden en la división?
hintsEs: No supongas que las dos divisiones son iguales: resuelve primero cada una por su cuenta.
Multiplica por el recíproco en las dos: invierte la segunda fracción cada vez y luego compara los dos cocientes.
La primera: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 → 3/4 × 2/1. Resuélvela y luego plantea 1/2 ÷ 3/4 igual y compara.

extending.label: Divide, then check your answer by multiplying: quotient × divisor should equal the dividend.
extending.hint: As the divisor decreases, does the quotient increase or decrease? Track the pattern.
hints: Each row pairs a division with a multiplication check — the check should rebuild the dividend.
Find the quotient by multiplying by the reciprocal, then multiply quotient × divisor to confirm.
Row one: 5/6 ÷ 1/3 → 5/6 × 3/1. Simplify it, then multiply your quotient by 1/3 — you should land back on 5/6.
extending.explanation: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 5/2, 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3, and 7/8 × 2/1 = 14/8 = 7/4. The check column multiplies each quotient back by its divisor — 5/2 × 1/3 = 5/6, 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9, and 7/4 × 1/2 = 7/8 — landing on the original dividend every time.
extending.explanationEs: Multiplicar por el recíproco da 5/6 × 3/1 = 15/6 = 5/2, 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3 y 7/8 × 2/1 = 14/8 = 7/4. La columna de comprobación multiplica cada cociente por su divisor —5/2 × 1/3 = 5/6, 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9 y 7/4 × 1/2 = 7/8— y cae en el dividendo original cada vez.
extending.labelEs: Divide y después comprueba tu respuesta multiplicando: cociente × divisor debe ser igual al dividendo.
hintsEs: Cada fila junta una división con una comprobación por multiplicación: la comprobación debe reconstruir el dividendo.
Halla el cociente multiplicando por el recíproco y luego multiplica cociente × divisor para confirmar.
Fila uno: 5/6 ÷ 1/3 → 5/6 × 3/1. Simplifícalo y luego multiplica tu cociente por 1/3: debes regresar a 5/6.

optionalActivity.name: Fraction Operation Lockbox
optionalActivity.intro: The evidence vault is sealed — divide each pair of fractions in simplest form and use your quotients to crack every lock.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5.
